title: introduce-resilient-dedicated-throttle-controller-and-percentile-throughput-reporter
author: Maya R. Chen
release_notes: Adds a DedicatedThrottleController to smooth burst allocations and a PercentileThroughputReporter metric for SLA visibility. Backwards compatible; config defaults preserve existing behavior. Operators should review new helm values documented in the release notes.
description: Motivation: Dedicated capacity customers need predictable throughput guarantees even during fleet-wide transient surges and node churn. Existing burst allocation logic can over-commit short-lived warm pools and create noisy percentile signals in observability. This PR introduces a DedicatedThrottleController, a small control-plane component that enforces soft per-tenant token smoothing, speculative backfill limits, and a drift-correction heuristic that prevents slow leak/accumulate behaviors when telemetry is sparse. The controller is configurable by tenant-level policy and integrated with the existing fleet headroom allocator so it can provide graceful degradation rather than hard rejects. We also add a PercentileThroughputReporter that computes 50/90/99 throughput percentiles for each tenant over sliding windows and emits both summary and raw-sample metrics for downstream reporting and SLO evaluation. Design highlights: 1) Token smoothing: uses a leaky-bucket style accumulator with a two-timescale smoothing (fast window for immediate burst allowance, slow window for baseline throughput) and an adjustable recovery factor to support graceful reduction after sustained high load. 2) Speculative backfill limiter: allows short-lived allocation from ephemeral warmlets but caps effective concurrency headroom per-tenant so large tenants cannot monopolize burst slots during cluster-wide surges. 3) Drift-correction heuristic: when the reporter detects steady mismatch between requested capacity and observed completions, the controller applies conservative calibration to the smoothing parameters to avoid runaway optimistic allocations. 4) Telemetry: the PercentileThroughputReporter emits per-tenant throughput percentiles (p50/p90/p99 tokens/sec), a burst-utilization ratio, and a 'smoothed_headroom' gauge used by autoscaler advisors. 5) Compatibility: new helm values default to disabled for clusters with custom schedulers; enabling requires setting dedicated.throttleController.enabled=true. Implementation notes: changes span controller code (pkg/controllers/dedicated_throttle.go), allocator integrations (pkg/allocator/headroom_adapter.go), telemetry (pkg/telemetry/percentile_reporter.go), a small operator CRD addition (deploy/crds/dedicatedpolicy.yaml), unit and e2e tests (pkg/controllers/*_test.go, test/e2e/dedicated_throttle_test.go), and chart values (charts/dedicated/values.yaml). Tests: added deterministic unit tests for smoothing math, three e2e scenarios that simulate short microbursts, sustained high load, and telemetry sparsity, plus a load harness run that asserts no regressions in 95th percentile latency. Observability: dashboards updated (observability/dashboards/dedicated_throttle.json) and a short runbook entry included (docs/ops/dedicated_throttle_runbook.md). Rollout plan: staged rollout behind the helm flag with canary percentage by tenant label; operator tooling will surface the new percentile metrics and suggestion engine will recommend knob values based on historical load. Backwards compatibility: controllers default to no-op if DedicatedPolicy CRD not present and helm flag is off. Related work: builds on ENG-1427 (headroom allocator refactor), leverages some heuristics from ENG-1683 (burst bank smoothing). Checklist: - [x] controller logic implemented - [x] allocator integration hooks - [x] unit + e2e tests - [x] telemetry + dashboards - [x] helm values + docs - [x] perf benchmark and no-regression check - [x] runbook and rollout notes

notes_for_ops: Enable with helm value dedicated.throttleController.enabled=true and set dedicated.throttleController.shardCount to match cluster size. Default backfillCap of 0.15 is conservative. Watch metrics: dedicated.throttle.smoothed_headroom, dedicated.throttle.burst_util_ratio,p50/p90/p99 throughput metrics. Rollback: toggle helm flag off and controller will drain; CRD remains but no enforcement occurs. If you see sustained negative drift alerts, increase slowWindowSeconds or reduce backfillCap.
upgrade_impact: Low: default behavior unchanged. Operators that enable the controller should run canary tenants first and validate percentile metrics. Helm chart bumped minor version and adds new values; automated upgrades will not enable the controller.
operational_runbook: Included in docs/ops/dedicated_throttle_runbook.md which covers detection (alerts on burst_util_ratio>0.9 for 10m), mitigation steps (lower backfillCap, increase slowWindowSeconds, scale shards), and rollback steps (helm toggle to disable). Also includes troubleshooting for telemetry sparsity and sample count thresholds.
notes: This PR intentionally keeps the enforcement soft — decisions are advisory to the autoscaler by default and become hard only when explicit policy backfillCap is set per-tenant. Future work: add adaptive recovery where the controller suggests knob updates to the Optimize engine and expose a control-plane API for temporary emergency lifts.
